docs.title: About Me
docs.text:
I am a First-Class Agricultural and Environmental Engineering graduate specializing in GIS, remote sensing, and geospatial data analysis. I use Google Earth Engine, QGIS, ArcGIS, Python, and statistical methods to investigate hydroclimatic trends, support climate resilience, assess environmental conditions, and identify suitable locations for agricultural infrastructure. My research interests focus on the intersection of geospatial science, sustainable agriculture, water resources, and environmental management. I am currently seeking GRA/GTA opportunities in geospatial analysis, remote sensing, and environmental or climate research where I can contribute my technical skills while advancing my research experience.

docs.title: 2025 Land Use/Land Cover Classification — Adansi South District
docs.text: 2025 LULC classification map for Adansi South District. The map displays six mapped classes: closed forest, open/degraded forest, cropland and fallow, mining/bare land, built-up areas, and water.

docs.title: Project overview
docs.text:
This Google Earth Engine (GEE) workflow maps land use and land cover (LULC) in Adansi South District, Ghana, for 2025. It uses Landsat 8 and Landsat 9 imagery and a Random Forest classifier to distinguish six land-cover classes.

The workflow is designed with two operating modes: a sample-picking mode for exploring predictor layers and potential training locations, and a classification mode for combining samples, training the model, producing the classified map, and exporting outputs.

docs.title: Land-cover classes
docs.text: Code Class Description 0 CCF Closed forest 1 ODF Open / degraded forest 2 CFL Cropland and fallow 3 MBL Mining / bare land 4 SET Built-up 5 WAT Water

docs.title: Imagery and predictor features
docs.text: The script uses Landsat 8 and 9 surface-reflectance imagery. Its predictor stack is designed to combine spectral information and derived features, including dry-season bands, spectral indices, a yearly NDVI profile, and texture information. The script's comments and settings describe a dry-season composite spanning November 2024 to February 2025.

docs.title: Workflow
docs.text:
1. Define or import the Adansi South District boundary (aoi).
  2. Prepare Landsat 8 and 9 imagery, including compositing and gap filling.
  3. Derive spectral indices and additional predictor features.
  4. In sample-picking mode, inspect predictor layers and potential sample locations for each class.
  5. Load training samples either from an uploaded table or from six class-specific sample layers.
  6. Train a Random Forest classifier and classify the study area.
  7. Generate class-area summaries and export the mapped results.

docs.title: Running the script
docs.text:
Open the JavaScript file in the Google Earth Engine Code Editor.

The script expects an imported district boundary named aoi. Depending on the selected sample workflow, it also expects either an uploaded table named samples with a numeric class field (values 0–5), or six sample layers named CCF, ODF, CFL, MBL, SET, and WAT.

The main settings at the beginning of the script control the workflow:

  • PICKING: set to true to inspect predictor layers and potential sample locations; set to false to run classification and exports.
  • USE_UPLOADED_TABLE: choose the uploaded sample table (true) or six separately imported/drawn class layers (false).
  • SAMPLE_GEOMETRY: specify whether uploaded samples are points or polygons.
  • POINTS_PER_POLYGON: number of random points generated within each training polygon.
  • START and END: date range used for the dry-season composite.

Check all imports and settings before running. The script's source comments provide further instructions for preparing the samples.

docs.title: Map interpretation
docs.text: The supplied map shows the spatial distribution of the six classes across the district. Closed forest (CCF) is represented in dark green, open/degraded forest (ODF) in light green, cropland and fallow (CFL) in yellow, mining/bare land (MBL) in brown, built-up areas (SET) in red, and water (WAT) in blue.

docs.title: Accuracy assessment and limitations
docs.text:
A classified map should not be treated as validated solely because it has been generated successfully. Before using the map in a report or decision-making process, review the script's accuracy-assessment outputs and document the sampling design, training/validation split, class-specific producer's and user's accuracies, overall accuracy, and any imbalance among classes.

Also consider:

  • Whether training and validation samples are independent and spatially representative.
  • Whether the dry-season image window is suitable for distinguishing seasonal cropland, fallow, and vegetation.
  • Whether mining/bare land and built-up areas are spectrally separable at the chosen spatial resolution.
  • Whether cloud, shadow, and image-gap handling leave artefacts in the composite.
  • Whether the map boundary, class definitions, and reference labels are appropriate for Adansi South District.

docs.title: JavaScript source
docs.text:
The complete script is available below and as a separate file for use in the GEE Code Editor.

//==================================================
// LULC 2025 - ADANSI SOUTH DISTRICT, GHANA
// Landsat 8 + 9 | Random Forest | 6 classes (values 0 to 5)
// Features: dry-season bands + indices + yearly NDVI profile + texture
//
// Built like the 2015 script: same compositing (with gap filling), same
// potential-site picking aid, same classification and area table.
//
// TWO MODES (see PICKING in Settings)
//   PICKING = true  : shows the bands, indices and extra features as map
//                     layers, plus POTENTIAL SITES for every class and
//                     suggested points, to make picking the samples easy.
//   PICKING = false : merges the samples, classifies and exports.
//
// IMPORTS NEEDED (create in the Code Editor, in THIS script)
// aoi : district boundary (table asset)
//
// SAMPLES: use ONE of the two options below
//   A) Uploaded table (from Google Earth Pro)  -> USE_UPLOADED_TABLE = true
//      Import the asset and name it "samples".
//      It needs a numeric field "class" (0 to 5). Points or polygons.
//   B) Six layers drawn in GEE                 -> USE_UPLOADED_TABLE = false
//      Name the layers CCF, ODF, CFL, MBL, SET, WAT.
//      Import them as FeatureCollection (gear icon -> Import as), or
//      as multi-point geometries (the script converts those).
//
// CLASS VALUES
//   0 = CCF  Closed forest
//   1 = ODF  Open / degraded forest
//   2 = CFL  Cropland and fallow
//   3 = MBL  Mining / bare land
//   4 = SET  Built-up
//   5 = WAT  Water
//==================================================

//==================================================
// Settings
//==================================================
var PICKING = false;             // true = picking layers + potential sites, false = run classification
var USE_UPLOADED_TABLE = false; // true = table "samples", false = six layers
var SAMPLE_GEOMETRY = "points"; // "points" or "polygons" (for the sample table)
var POINTS_PER_POLYGON = 15;    // random points made inside each polygon

var START = "2024-11-01";       // dry season composite: Nov 2024 - Feb 2025
var END = "2025-03-01";
var ADD_NEXT_SEASON = false;    // true = also use Nov 2025 - Feb 2026 scenes (fills gaps)
var NEXT_START = "2025-11-01";
var NEXT_END = "2026-03-01";
var PHENO_START = "2024-11-01"; // 12 months used for the yearly NDVI profile
var PHENO_END = "2025-11-01";
var USE_L8 = true;              // Landsat 8 scenes
var USE_L9 = true;              // Landsat 9 scenes (available since 2021)
var FILL_GAPS = true;           // fill cloud gaps from a 12-month composite + neighbours

var N_TREES = 200;
var TRAIN_FRACTION = 0.7;       // 70 % train / 30 % test
var MIN_DISTANCE = 100;         // metres between test and train points (points only)
var CRS = "EPSG:32630";         // UTM zone 30N

// After the first run, put weak bands from "Variable importance" here
// to drop them, for example ["EVI", "NDWI"]
var DROP_BANDS = [];

// class names (used in the legend and the area table)
var classNames = [
  "0 Closed forest",
  "1 Open / degraded forest",
  "2 Cropland and fallow",
  "3 Mining / bare land",
  "4 Built-up",
  "5 Water",
];

var PALETTE = ["0b4f1a", "7cb342", "f5d76e", "b0703c", "d32f2f", "1e88e5"];
var classCodes = ["CCF", "ODF", "CFL", "MBL", "SET", "WAT"];

//--------------------------------------------------
// Potential-site settings (picking aid, PICKING = true)
// The thresholds are STARTING VALUES. Click known places with the Inspector
// and adjust them. The console prints the area of each potential class:
// 0 ha = rule too strict, very large = rule too loose.
//--------------------------------------------------
var EPOCH = 2025;              // used for the Hansen forest-loss cut-off year
                               // (the Hansen dataset used here ends in 2023, so for 2025
                               // it flags every loss up to 2023)
var USE_WORLDCOVER = true;     // use ESA WorldCover (2020) for cropland and built-up
                               // (2020 map: new farms and buildings since then are missed)
var N_SUGGEST = 200;           // suggested points per class
var EXPORT_SUGGESTIONS = true; // export suggested points as KML (Google Earth Pro)
//
// ONE SIMPLE RULE PER CLASS (all conditions must hold)
//   0 CCF  NDVI > 0.65, NDMI > 0.25, smooth texture, Hansen tree cover >= 70 %
//   1 ODF  NDVI 0.40-0.70, NDMI 0.10-0.30, Hansen tree cover >= 30 %
//   2 CFL  NDVI 0.20-0.60, not bare (BSI < 0.1), not wet (MNDWI < 0),
//          some seasonal change, and (WorldCover cropland OR clearly non-forest)
//   3 MBL  BSI > 0.1, NDVI < 0.25, MNDWI < 0.1, not a settlement
//          + muddy ponds (MNDWI > 0, RED > GREEN, not permanent water)
//   4 SET  WorldCover built-up share >= 30 % of the cell, NDVI < 0.45
//   5 WAT  MNDWI > 0, NDVI < 0.15, and not a muddy mining pond
//
var MIN_CLASS_HA = 40;         // warn if a potential class is smaller than this
// erode = keep only the core of each patch (3 x 3 pixels = 90 m).
// Only forests are eroded: rivers, fields, mines and settlements are too small.
var ERODE = { ccf: true, odf: true, cfl: false, mbl: false, set: false, wat: false };
var T = {
  ccf: { ndvi: 0.65, ndmi: 0.25, std: 0.06, p10: 0.45, cover: 70 },
  odf: { ndviMin: 0.4, ndviMax: 0.7, ndmiMin: 0.1, ndmiMax: 0.3, cover: 30 },
  cfl: { ndviMin: 0.2, ndviMax: 0.6, bsiMax: 0.1, range: 0.15, rangeStrong: 0.25,
         coverMax: 30, wcFrac: 0.5 },
  mbl: { bsi: 0.1, ndviMax: 0.25, mndwiMax: 0.1 },
  pond: { mndwi: 0.0, ndti: 0.0, gswMax: 50, ndviMax: 0.15 }, // muddy, non-permanent water
  set: { ndbi: 0.0, ndviMax: 0.45, wcFrac: 0.3 },
  wat: { mndwi: 0.0, ndviMax: 0.15 },
};

// visualization parameters for the composite
var rgb_viz = { bands: ["RED", "GREEN", "BLUE"], min: 0.02, max: 0.25 };

//==================================================
// Landsat imagery filter
//==================================================
var l8 = ee.ImageCollection("LANDSAT/LC08/C02/T1_L2");
var l9 = ee.ImageCollection("LANDSAT/LC09/C02/T1_L2");
var landsat = USE_L8 && USE_L9 ? l8.merge(l9) : USE_L9 ? l9 : l8;

var dateFilter = ADD_NEXT_SEASON
  ? ee.Filter.or(
      ee.Filter.date(START, END),
      ee.Filter.date(NEXT_START, NEXT_END)
    )
  : ee.Filter.date(START, END);

//dataset filter (dry season)
var scenes = landsat
  .filter(dateFilter)
  // Optional: pre-filter to get less cloudy scenes.
  // .filter(ee.Filter.lt("CLOUD_COVER", 50))
  .filterBounds(aoi);
print("Scenes used (dry season)", scenes.size());
scenes.size().evaluate(function (n) {
  if (n === 0) {
    print("NO SCENES FOUND: check START/END, USE_L8 and USE_L9.");
  }
});

// cloud-masked, scaled scenes
var yearScenes = landsat.filterDate(PHENO_START, PHENO_END).filterBounds(aoi);
var dryMasked = scenes.map(maskLandsatClouds);
var yearMasked = yearScenes.map(maskLandsatClouds);

var dryRaw = dryMasked.median(); // may have gaps (cloud in every scene)
var validFrac = function (img) {
  return img
    .select("SR_B4")
    .mask()
    .reduceRegion({
      reducer: ee.Reducer.mean(),
      geometry: aoi.geometry(),
      scale: 30,
      maxPixels: 1e13,
    })
    .get("SR_B4");
};
print("Valid-pixel fraction, dry season BEFORE filling", validFrac(dryRaw));

var filled = dryRaw;
if (FILL_GAPS) {
  // fill 1: use the 12-month composite where the dry season has a gap
  // fill 2: fill small remaining holes from their neighbours
  filled = dryRaw.unmask(yearMasked.median()).reproject({ crs: CRS, scale: 30 });
  filled = filled.unmask(
    filled.focalMedian({ radius: 3, units: "pixels", kernelType: "square" })
  );
}
filled = filled.clip(aoi);
print("Valid-pixel fraction AFTER filling", validFrac(filled));

var imagery = selectBands(filled);

//==================================================
// Extra features: yearly NDVI profile and texture
//==================================================
// NDVI low / median / high over 12 months separates crops (strong seasonal
// change) from forest (stable) better than the dry season alone.
var yearCol = yearMasked.map(function (img) {
  return img.normalizedDifference(["SR_B5", "SR_B4"]).rename("NDVI");
});
print("Scenes used (yearly profile)", yearCol.size());

var ndviP = yearCol.reduce(ee.Reducer.percentile([10, 50, 90]));
var ndviRange = ndviP
  .select("NDVI_p90")
  .subtract(ndviP.select("NDVI_p10"))
  .rename("NDVI_range");

// Texture: local variation of NDVI (forest is smooth, farms are patchy)
var ndviStd = imagery
  .select("NDVI")
  .reduceNeighborhood({
    reducer: ee.Reducer.stdDev(),
    kernel: ee.Kernel.square(1),
  })
  .rename("NDVI_std");

imagery = imagery
  .addBands([ndviP, ndviRange, ndviStd])
  .reproject({ crs: CRS, scale: 30 })
  .clip(aoi);

var inputBands = imagery.bandNames().removeAll(DROP_BANDS);
print("Bands used", inputBands);


// visualize imagery
Map.centerObject(aoi, 11);
Map.addLayer(imagery, rgb_viz, "True colour (B4, B3, B2)", true);
Map.addLayer(
  dryRaw.select("SR_B4").mask().not().selfMask().clip(aoi),
  { palette: ["ff00ff"] },
  "Dry-season gaps that were filled",
  false
);

//==================================================
// Layers for picking points (PICKING = true)
// Turn them on and off in the Layers menu (top right of the map).
// Use the Inspector tab to read the values at a clicked point.
//==================================================
if (PICKING) {
  Map.setOptions("SATELLITE"); // high-resolution basemap to compare with

  // show the uploaded samples to check them
  if (USE_UPLOADED_TABLE) {
    Map.addLayer(samples, { color: "ff00ff" }, "samples (uploaded)", false);
  }

  // colour composites
  Map.addLayer(
    imagery,
    { bands: ["SWIR1", "NIR", "RED"], min: 0.02, max: 0.4 },
    "False colour (B6, B5, B4)",
    false
  );
  Map.addLayer(
    imagery,
    { bands: ["NIR", "RED", "GREEN"], min: 0.02, max: 0.45 },
    "Vegetation colour (B5, B4, B3)",
    false
  );

  // single bands in grey: [band, layer name, max reflectance]
  var bandLayers = [
    ["BLUE", "B2 Blue", 0.15],
    ["GREEN", "B3 Green", 0.2],
    ["RED", "B4 Red", 0.25],
    ["NIR", "B5 NIR", 0.5],
    ["SWIR1", "B6 SWIR1", 0.4],
    ["SWIR2", "B7 SWIR2", 0.3],
  ];
  bandLayers.forEach(function (b) {
    Map.addLayer(
      imagery.select(b[0]),
      { min: 0, max: b[2], palette: ["000000", "ffffff"] },
      b[1],
      false
    );
  });

  // palettes
  var vegPal = ["d73027", "fee08b", "1a9850"];
  var waterPal = ["8c510a", "f5f5f5", "2166ac"];
  var builtPal = ["2166ac", "f5f5f5", "b2182b"];
  var soilPal = ["1a9850", "fee08b", "8c510a"];
  var moistPal = ["8c510a", "f5f5f5", "01665e"];
  var greyPal = ["ffffff", "000000"];

  // indices and extra features: [band, min, max, palette]
  var indexLayers = [
    ["NDVI", -0.2, 0.9, vegPal],
    ["EVI", 0, 1, vegPal],
    ["NDMI", -0.3, 0.5, moistPal],
    ["NBR", -0.2, 0.8, vegPal],
    ["NDWI", -0.6, 0.6, waterPal],
    ["MNDWI", -0.6, 0.6, waterPal],
    ["NDBI", -0.5, 0.3, builtPal],
    ["BSI", -0.4, 0.3, soilPal],
    ["slope", 0, 20, greyPal],
    ["NDVI_p10", -0.2, 0.8, vegPal],
    ["NDVI_p50", -0.2, 0.9, vegPal],
    ["NDVI_p90", -0.2, 0.9, vegPal],
    ["NDVI_range", 0, 0.6, greyPal],
    ["NDVI_std", 0, 0.15, greyPal],
  ];
  indexLayers.forEach(function (x) {
    Map.addLayer(
      imagery.select(x[0]),
      { min: x[1], max: x[2], palette: x[3] },
      x[0],
      false
    );
  });

  //==================================================
  // POTENTIAL SITES FOR EACH CLASS (picking aid)
  // Rule-based "likely" areas. They are only suggestions: confirm each
  // place on the satellite basemap before you place a point.
  //==================================================
  var yy = EPOCH - 2000; // Hansen loss-year code of the epoch (2025 -> 25)
  var gfc = ee.Image("UMD/hansen/global_forest_change_2023_v1_11");
  var cover = gfc.select("treecover2000");
  var lossYear = gfc.select("lossyear");
  var notLostYet = lossYear.eq(0).or(lossYear.gt(yy)); // forest still standing
  var lostByEpoch = lossYear.gte(1).and(lossYear.lte(yy)); // cleared before the epoch
  var wc = ee.ImageCollection("ESA/WorldCover/v100").first().select("Map");
  var gsw = ee.Image("JRC/GSW1_4/GlobalSurfaceWater")
    .select("occurrence")
    .unmask(0);

  var band = function (name) {
    return imagery.select(name);
  };

  // share of each 30 m cell covered by a WorldCover class (10 m map, 2020)
  var wcFrac = function (code) {
    return wc
      .eq(code)
      .reduceResolution({ reducer: ee.Reducer.mean(), maxPixels: 1024 })
      .reproject({ crs: CRS, scale: 30 });
  };
  var wcCrop = wcFrac(40);
  var wcBuilt = wcFrac(50);

  // turbidity: muddy water has RED >= GREEN
  var ndti = band("RED")
    .subtract(band("GREEN"))
    .divide(band("RED").add(band("GREEN")));

  // 0 Closed forest
  var ccfRaw = band("NDVI").gt(T.ccf.ndvi)
    .and(band("NDMI").gt(T.ccf.ndmi))
    .and(band("NDVI_std").lt(T.ccf.std))
    .and(band("NDVI_p10").gt(T.ccf.p10))
    .and(cover.gte(T.ccf.cover))
    .and(notLostYet);

  // 1 Open / degraded forest
  var odfRaw = band("NDVI").gte(T.odf.ndviMin)
    .and(band("NDVI").lte(T.odf.ndviMax))
    .and(band("NDMI").gte(T.odf.ndmiMin))
    .and(band("NDMI").lte(T.odf.ndmiMax))
    .and(cover.gte(T.odf.cover))
    .and(lostByEpoch.not());

  // 2 Cropland and fallow: green but not forest, not bare, not wet,
  //   with some seasonal change; supported by WorldCover cropland or by a
  //   strong seasonal change outside forest
  var cflSupport = band("NDVI_range").gt(T.cfl.rangeStrong)
    .and(cover.lt(T.cfl.coverMax).or(lostByEpoch));
  if (USE_WORLDCOVER) {
    cflSupport = cflSupport.or(wcCrop.gte(T.cfl.wcFrac));
  }
  var cflRaw = band("NDVI").gte(T.cfl.ndviMin)
    .and(band("NDVI").lte(T.cfl.ndviMax))
    .and(band("BSI").lt(T.cfl.bsiMax))
    .and(band("MNDWI").lt(0))
    .and(band("NDVI_range").gt(T.cfl.range))
    .and(cflSupport);

  // 3 Mining / bare land: bare spoil, plus muddy non-permanent ponds
  var spoil = band("BSI").gt(T.mbl.bsi)
    .and(band("NDVI").lt(T.mbl.ndviMax))
    .and(band("MNDWI").lt(T.mbl.mndwiMax));
  if (USE_WORLDCOVER) {
    spoil = spoil.and(wcBuilt.lt(T.set.wcFrac)); // keep settlements out of mining
  }
  var pond = band("MNDWI").gt(T.pond.mndwi)
    .and(ndti.gt(T.pond.ndti))
    .and(gsw.lt(T.pond.gswMax))
    .and(band("NDVI").lt(T.pond.ndviMax));
  var mblRaw = spoil.or(pond);

  // 4 Built-up: WorldCover built-up share of the cell, little vegetation.
  //   Without WorldCover: high NDBI, little vegetation, not bare spoil.
  var setRaw = USE_WORLDCOVER
    ? wcBuilt.gte(T.set.wcFrac).and(band("NDVI").lt(T.set.ndviMax))
    : band("NDBI").gt(T.set.ndbi)
        .and(band("NDVI").lt(T.set.ndviMax))
        .and(band("BSI").lt(T.mbl.bsi))
        .and(band("MNDWI").lt(0));

  // 5 Water: open water that is not a muddy mining pond
  var watRaw = band("MNDWI").gt(T.wat.mndwi)
    .and(band("NDVI").lt(T.wat.ndviMax))
    .and(pond.not());

  // keep the core of each patch (3 x 3 pixels) where requested
  var core = function (raw, erode) {
    raw = raw.reproject({ crs: CRS, scale: 30 });
    return erode
      ? raw.focalMin({ radius: 1, units: "pixels", kernelType: "square" })
      : raw;
  };

  // one image of potential classes (later entries are drawn on top, so the
  // small classes win over the forests where rules overlap)
  var parts = [
    [1, core(odfRaw, ERODE.odf)],
    [2, core(cflRaw, ERODE.cfl)],
    [0, core(ccfRaw, ERODE.ccf)],
    [4, core(setRaw, ERODE.set)],
    [3, core(mblRaw, ERODE.mbl)],
    [5, core(watRaw, ERODE.wat)],
  ];
  var cand = ee
    .ImageCollection(
      parts.map(function (p) {
        return ee.Image(p[0]).updateMask(p[1]).rename("class").toByte();
      })
    )
    .mosaic();

  Map.addLayer(
    cand,
    { min: 0, max: 5, palette: PALETTE },
    "Potential sites (all classes)",
    true
  );
  for (var v = 0; v < 6; v++) {
    Map.addLayer(
      cand.updateMask(cand.eq(v)),
      { palette: [PALETTE[v]] },
      "Potential: " + classNames[v],
      false
    );
  }


  // ---- Simple helper layers (one rule each), to pick points quickly ----
  // They also catch look-alikes, so confirm each spot on the satellite basemap.

  // Mining / bare land: bare, non-green, not water, not a settlement
  Map.addLayer(
    spoil.selfMask(),
    { palette: ["ff00ff"] },
    "Mining candidates (check on satellite)",
    false
  );

  // Farmland: moderately green, not bare, not wet, seasonal change, gentle
  // slope, and not forest
  var farmCandidate = band("NDVI").gte(T.cfl.ndviMin)
    .and(band("NDVI").lte(T.cfl.ndviMax))
    .and(band("BSI").lt(T.cfl.bsiMax))
    .and(band("MNDWI").lt(0))
    .and(band("NDVI_range").gt(T.cfl.range))
    .and(band("slope").lt(15))
    .and(cover.lt(50).or(lostByEpoch));
  Map.addLayer(
    farmCandidate.selfMask(),
    { palette: ["ffa500"] },
    "Farmland candidates (check on satellite)",
    false
  );

  // Stronger farmland: the rule above AND WorldCover cropland covers at
  // least half of the 30 m cell
  var farmStrong = farmCandidate.and(wcCrop.gte(T.cfl.wcFrac));
  Map.addLayer(
    farmStrong.selfMask(),
    { palette: ["ff0000"] },
    "Farmland candidates, strong (WorldCover cropland)",
    false
  );

  // Fallow / regrowth: forest cleared earlier and now medium green
  var fallowCandidate = band("NDVI").gte(0.3)
    .and(band("NDVI").lte(0.65))
    .and(band("BSI").lt(T.cfl.bsiMax))
    .and(cover.gte(30))
    .and(lostByEpoch);
  Map.addLayer(
    fallowCandidate.selfMask(),
    { palette: ["00bcd4"] },
    "Fallow / regrowth candidates (check on satellite)",
    false
  );

  // area of each helper layer (ha): 0 = too strict, huge = too loose
  print(
    "Helper area (ha): mining, farm, strong, fallow",
    ee.Image.cat([
      spoil.rename("mining"),
      farmCandidate.rename("farm"),
      farmStrong.rename("strong"),
      fallowCandidate.rename("fallow"),
    ])
      .multiply(ee.Image.pixelArea().divide(10000))
      .reduceRegion({
        reducer: ee.Reducer.sum(),
        geometry: aoi.geometry(),
        scale: 30,
        crs: CRS,
        maxPixels: 1e13,
        tileScale: 8,
      })
  );

  // area of each potential class (check that no rule is empty or too wide)
  var candArea = ee.Image.cat(
    [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5].map(function (k) {
      return cand.eq(k).rename("c" + k);
    })
  )
    .multiply(ee.Image.pixelArea().divide(10000))
    .reduceRegion({
      reducer: ee.Reducer.sum(),
      geometry: aoi.geometry(),
      scale: 30,
      crs: CRS,
      maxPixels: 1e13,
      tileScale: 8,
    });
  print("Potential-site area (ha): c0 CCF, c1 ODF, c2 CFL, c3 MBL, c4 SET, c5 WAT", candArea);
  candArea.evaluate(function (d) {
    [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5].forEach(function (k) {
      var ha = d && d["c" + k] ? d["c" + k] : 0;
      if (ha < MIN_CLASS_HA) {
        print(
          "WARNING: potential area of " + classNames[k] + " is only " + Math.round(ha) +
            " ha. Relax its rule in T (Settings)."
        );
      }
    });
  });

  // suggested points inside the potential sites
  var nPts = [N_SUGGEST, N_SUGGEST, N_SUGGEST, N_SUGGEST, N_SUGGEST, N_SUGGEST];
  var suggest = cand.stratifiedSample({
    numPoints: 0,
    classBand: "class",
    region: aoi.geometry(),
    scale: 30,
    projection: ee.Projection(CRS),
    seed: 7,
    classValues: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5],
    classPoints: nPts,
    geometries: true,
    tileScale: 4,
  });
  print("Suggested points per class", suggest.aggregate_histogram("class"));

  for (var w = 0; w < 6; w++) {
    Map.addLayer(
      suggest.filter(ee.Filter.eq("class", w)),
      { color: PALETTE[w] },
      "Suggested points: " + classNames[w],
      false
    );
    if (EXPORT_SUGGESTIONS) {
      Export.table.toDrive({
        collection: suggest.filter(ee.Filter.eq("class", w)),
        description: "Suggested_" + classCodes[w] + "_" + EPOCH,
        folder: "LULC",
        fileFormat: "KML",
      });
    }
  }

  print(
    "PICKING mode: use the Potential sites layers to place your points, " +
      "then set PICKING = false to classify."
  );
}

//==================================================
// Classification (PICKING = false)
//==================================================
if (!PICKING) {
  //===================================================
  // Machine Learning Model
  //===================================================
  //class layers: from the uploaded table, or from the six drawn layers
  var layers = USE_UPLOADED_TABLE
    ? [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5].map(function (v) {
        return samples.filter(ee.Filter.eq("class", v));
      })
    : [CCF, ODF, CFL, MBL, SET, WAT];

  //merge samples (each layer gets its class value 0 to 5)
  var sample = setClass(layers[0], 0)
    .merge(setClass(layers[1], 1))
    .merge(setClass(layers[2], 2))
    .merge(setClass(layers[3], 3))
    .merge(setClass(layers[4], 4))
    .merge(setClass(layers[5], 5));

  print("Samples per class (all)", sample.aggregate_histogram("class"));

  // split train and test (70 / 30)
  var train = sample.filter(ee.Filter.lte("random", TRAIN_FRACTION));
  var test = sample.filter(ee.Filter.gt("random", TRAIN_FRACTION));

  if (SAMPLE_GEOMETRY === "polygons" && USE_UPLOADED_TABLE) {
    // the split is by polygon, so train and test never share a polygon;
    // then random points are made inside each polygon
    train = polygonsToPoints(train);
    test = polygonsToPoints(test);
  } else {
    // remove test points closer than 100 m to any training point
    var near = ee.Filter.withinDistance({
      distance: MIN_DISTANCE,
      leftField: ".geo",
      rightField: ".geo",
      maxError: 1,
    });
    test = ee.FeatureCollection(ee.Join.inverted().apply(test, train, near));
  }

  print("Training points per class", train.aggregate_histogram("class"));
  print("Test points per class", test.aggregate_histogram("class"));

  // Extract image values
  var trainSample = imagery.select(inputBands).sampleRegions({
    collection: train,
    scale: 30,
    properties: ["class"],
    tileScale: 4,
  });
  var testSample = imagery.select(inputBands).sampleRegions({
    collection: test,
    scale: 30,
    properties: ["class"],
    tileScale: 4,
  });

  // Legend dict
  var legendInfo = {
    LULC_class_values: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5],
    LULC_class_palette: PALETTE,
  };

  // Train rf model
  var rf_model = ee.Classifier.smileRandomForest({
    numberOfTrees: N_TREES,
    seed: 42,
  }).train({
    features: trainSample,
    classProperty: "class",
    inputProperties: inputBands,
  });

  // Which bands matter most
  print(
    "Variable importance",
    ee.Dictionary(rf_model.explain()).get("importance")
  );

  // Training accuracy: compare with the test accuracy below.
  // Training much higher than test = memorising (mixed / near-duplicate points).
  var trainCM = trainSample
    .classify(rf_model, "predict")
    .errorMatrix("class", "predict", [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]);
  print("Training accuracy", trainCM.accuracy());

  // Accuracy test
  var cm = testSample
    .classify(rf_model, "predict")
    .errorMatrix("class", "predict", [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5]);
  print("Confusion matrix", cm, "Accuracy", cm.accuracy(), "Kappa", cm.kappa());
  print("Producer accuracy", cm.producersAccuracy());
  print("User accuracy", cm.consumersAccuracy());

  //==================================================
  // Misclassified test points (where the confusion is)
  // Colour of each point = its TRUE class (same colours as the legend).
  // Click a point with the Inspector: "class" = true class, "predict" = predicted.
  //==================================================
  var testPred = imagery
    .select(inputBands)
    .sampleRegions({
      collection: test,
      scale: 30,
      properties: ["class"],
      geometries: true,
      tileScale: 4,
    })
    .classify(rf_model, "predict");

  var wrong = testPred
    .map(function (f) {
      return f.set(
        "wrong",
        ee.Number(f.get("class")).neq(ee.Number(f.get("predict")))
      );
    })
    .filter(ee.Filter.eq("wrong", 1));

  var wrongStyled = wrong.map(function (f) {
    var color = ee.List(legendInfo.LULC_class_palette).get(
      ee.Number(f.get("class")).int()
    );
    return f.set(
      "style",
      ee.Dictionary({ color: color, pointSize: 7, pointShape: "circle" })
    );
  });

  Map.addLayer(
    wrongStyled.style({ styleProperty: "style" }),
    {},
    "Misclassified test points (colour = true class)",
    true
  );
  print("Number of misclassified test points", wrong.size());
  print("Misclassified points (class = true, predict = predicted)", wrong.limit(50));

  // Export the wrong points to check them in ArcGIS / Google Earth
  Export.table.toDrive({
    collection: wrong,
    description: "Misclassified_points_2025",
    folder: "LULC",
    fileFormat: "SHP",
  });

  // Classify, then 3 x 3 majority filter to remove isolated pixels
  var lulc = imagery
    .select(inputBands)
    .classify(rf_model, "LULC")
    .focalMode({ radius: 1, units: "pixels", kernelType: "square" })
    .toByte()
    .clip(aoi)
    .set(legendInfo);
  Map.addLayer(lulc, {}, "lulc", true);

  // Area per class (ha). Every class 0 to 5 is listed, with 0 ha if the
  // class has no pixels, so a missing class (for example mining) is visible.
  var classMasks = ee.Image.cat(
    [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5].map(function (v) {
      return lulc.eq(v).rename("c" + v);
    })
  );
  var areaDict = classMasks
    .multiply(ee.Image.pixelArea().divide(10000))
    .reduceRegion({
      reducer: ee.Reducer.sum(),
      geometry: aoi.geometry(),
      scale: 30,
      crs: CRS,
      maxPixels: 1e13,
      tileScale: 8,
    });

  var areaRaw = ee.FeatureCollection(
    [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5].map(function (v) {
      return ee.Feature(null, {
        class_value: v,
        class_name: classNames[v],
        area_ha: areaDict.get("c" + v),
      });
    })
  );
  var totalHa = ee.Number(areaRaw.aggregate_sum("area_ha"));
  var areaTable = areaRaw.map(function (f) {
    return f.set(
      "percent",
      ee.Number(f.get("area_ha")).divide(totalHa).multiply(100)
    );
  });
  print("Area per class (ha and %)", areaTable);
  print("Total mapped area (ha)", totalHa);
  print(
    ui.Chart.feature
      .byFeature(areaTable, "class_name", "area_ha")
      .setChartType("ColumnChart")
      .setOptions({
        title: "Area per class (ha), 2025",
        legend: { position: "none" },
        hAxis: { title: "Class" },
        vAxis: { title: "Hectares" },
      })
  );

  // The CSV export runs as a task, so it works even if the console is slow
  Export.table.toDrive({
    collection: areaTable,
    description: "LULC_2025_area_per_class",
    folder: "LULC",
    fileFormat: "CSV",
  });

  //==================================================
  // Legend
  //==================================================
  // set position of panel
  var legend = ui.Panel({
    style: {
      position: "bottom-left",
      padding: "8px 15px",
    },
  });

  // Create legend title
  var legendTitle = ui.Label({
    value: "LULC 2025",
    style: {
      fontWeight: "bold",
      fontSize: "18px",
      margin: "0 0 4px 0",
      padding: "0",
    },
  });

  // Add the title to the panel
  legend.add(legendTitle);

  // Creates and styles 1 row of the legend.
  var makeRow = function (color, name) {
    // Create the label that is actually the colored box.
    var colorBox = ui.Label({
      style: {
        backgroundColor: "#" + color,
        // Use padding to give the box height and width.
        padding: "8px",
        margin: "0 0 4px 0",
      },
    });

    // Create the label filled with the description text.
    var description = ui.Label({
      value: name,
      style: { margin: "0 0 4px 6px" },
    });

    // return the panel
    return ui.Panel({
      widgets: [colorBox, description],
      layout: ui.Panel.Layout.Flow("horizontal"),
    });
  };

  //  Palette with the colors
  var palette = legendInfo.LULC_class_palette;

  // Add color and names
  for (var i = 0; i < classNames.length; i++) {
    legend.add(makeRow(palette[i], classNames[i]));
  }

  // add legend to map (alternatively you can also print the legend to the console)
  Map.add(legend);

  // Export lulc to google drive
  Export.image.toDrive({
    image: lulc,
    scale: 30,
    region: aoi.geometry(),
    crs: CRS,
    maxPixels: 1e13,
    folder: "LULC",
    description: "LULC_2025_AdansiSouth",
    formatOptions: {
      cloudOptimized: true,
    },
  });
}

//==================================================
// Filter Cloud Landsat 8 / 9
//==================================================

function maskLandsatClouds(image) {
  var qa = image.select("QA_PIXEL");

  // Bits 1, 2, 3 and 4 are dilated cloud, cirrus, cloud and cloud shadow.
  var dilatedBitMask = 1 << 1;
  var cirrusBitMask = 1 << 2;
  var cloudBitMask = 1 << 3;
  var shadowBitMask = 1 << 4;

  // All flags should be set to zero, indicating clear conditions.
  var mask = qa
    .bitwiseAnd(dilatedBitMask)
    .eq(0)
    .and(qa.bitwiseAnd(cirrusBitMask).eq(0))
    .and(qa.bitwiseAnd(cloudBitMask).eq(0))
    .and(qa.bitwiseAnd(shadowBitMask).eq(0));

  // Scale the surface reflectance bands (Collection 2 Level 2)
  var sr = image.select("SR_B.").multiply(0.0000275).add(-0.2);

  return sr.updateMask(mask);
}

//========================================================================
// function to select the required bands and add the indices and slope
//========================================================================
function selectBands(image) {
  //required bands selection
  var bands = ["SR_B2", "SR_B3", "SR_B4", "SR_B5", "SR_B6", "SR_B7"];
  var names = ["BLUE", "GREEN", "RED", "NIR", "SWIR1", "SWIR2"];
  image = image.select(bands, names);

  // vegetation
  var ndvi = image.normalizedDifference(["NIR", "RED"]).rename("NDVI");

  var evi = image
    .expression("2.5 * (NIR - RED) / (NIR + 6 * RED - 7.5 * BLUE + 1)", {
      NIR: image.select("NIR"),
      RED: image.select("RED"),
      BLUE: image.select("BLUE"),
    })
    .rename("EVI");

  // moisture and burn / disturbance
  var ndmi = image.normalizedDifference(["NIR", "SWIR1"]).rename("NDMI");
  var nbr = image.normalizedDifference(["NIR", "SWIR2"]).rename("NBR");

  // water
  var ndwi = image.normalizedDifference(["GREEN", "NIR"]).rename("NDWI");
  var mndwi = image.normalizedDifference(["GREEN", "SWIR1"]).rename("MNDWI");

  // built-up and bare soil
  var ndbi = image.normalizedDifference(["SWIR1", "NIR"]).rename("NDBI");

  var bsi = image
    .expression(
      "((SWIR1 + RED) - (NIR + BLUE)) / ((SWIR1 + RED) + (NIR + BLUE))",
      {
        SWIR1: image.select("SWIR1"),
        RED: image.select("RED"),
        NIR: image.select("NIR"),
        BLUE: image.select("BLUE"),
      }
    )
    .rename("BSI");

  // terrain
  var slope = ee.Terrain.slope(ee.Image("USGS/SRTMGL1_003")).rename("slope").clip(aoi);

  // add the indices and slope to the image
  image = image.addBands(
    ee.Image([ndvi, evi, ndmi, nbr, ndwi, mndwi, ndbi, bsi, slope])
  );
  return image;
}

//========================================================================
// make sure a sample layer is a FeatureCollection. Layers drawn in GEE are
// imported as Geometry by default; a multi-point geometry is converted to
// one feature per point. (Polygon or single-point layers: change the
// import type to FeatureCollection with the gear icon in the Imports panel.)
//========================================================================
function toFC(x) {
  if (x instanceof ee.FeatureCollection) return x;
  return ee.FeatureCollection(
    ee.List(ee.Geometry(x).coordinates()).map(function (c) {
      return ee.Feature(ee.Geometry.Point(c));
    })
  );
}

//========================================================================
// function to give each sample layer its class value and a random column
// (the random column is made per class, so the 70 / 30 split is by class)
//========================================================================
function setClass(fc, value) {
  return toFC(fc)
    .map(function (f) {
      return f.set("class", value);
    })
    .randomColumn("random", 42);
}

//========================================================================
// function to make random points inside each polygon (keeps the class)
//========================================================================
function polygonsToPoints(polys) {
  var pts = polys.toList(polys.size()).map(function (f) {
    f = ee.Feature(f);
    return ee.FeatureCollection.randomPoints({
      region: f.geometry(),
      points: POINTS_PER_POLYGON,
      seed: 42,
      maxError: 1,
    }).map(function (p) {
      return p.set("class", f.get("class"));
    });
  });
  return ee.FeatureCollection(pts).flatten();
}

docs.text: This section presents geospatial analysis workflows developed with Google Earth Engine (GEE).

docs.title: Featured analysis
docs.text:
• RUSLE Soil Loss and Erosion Risk Mapping — estimates potential annual soil loss using the Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE), maps erosion-severity classes, and exports raster outputs.

Each project page includes the objective, workflow, datasets, key settings, example output, and JavaScript source code.

Research note: Model outputs are estimates. Review the assumptions, input data, spatial resolution, and local calibration requirements before using results for decisions.

docs.title: Project overview
docs.text:
This Google Earth Engine (GEE) workflow implements the Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (RUSLE) to estimate potential average annual soil loss:

[ A = R \times K \times LS \times C \times P ]

where (A) is estimated soil loss (t ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹), (R) is rainfall erosivity, (K) is soil erodibility, (LS) represents slope length and steepness, (C) represents cover-management, and (P) represents support practices.

The script creates factor layers, an estimated soil-loss map, erosion-severity classes, summary statistics, and Google Drive export tasks.

docs.title: Data and methods
docs.text: Component Source or method Role Rainfall erosivity ((R)) CHIRPS daily precipitation; Modified Fournier Index and Renard–Freimund relationship Estimates rainfall erosivity Soil erodibility ((K)) OpenLandMap sand, clay, and organic-carbon layers; EPIC-style equation Represents soil susceptibility to detachment Slope factor ((LS)) MERIT Hydro elevation and upstream area; Moore–Burch formulation Represents terrain effects Cover-management ((C)) ESA WorldCover lookup table or Sentinel-2 NDVI option Represents land-cover protection Support practice ((P)) (P=1) by default, with an optional slope-based cropland parameterization Represents conservation-practice assumptions

docs.title: Main outputs
docs.text:
• Estimated annual soil loss raster (A, t/ha/yr).
  • Six-category erosion-severity raster.
  • Individual (R), (K), (LS), (C), and (P) factor layers.
  • Mean, median, and maximum estimated soil loss.
  • Estimated total soil loss and area by erosion class.
  • Google Drive export tasks for the soil-loss map, classes, and factor stack.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Edit the settings near the beginning of the script before running it in the Google Earth Engine Code Editor.

  • aoi: replace the example rectangle with your study-area boundary.
  • RAIN_START_YEAR and RAIN_END_YEAR: define the rainfall averaging period.
  • C_METHOD: choose 'landcover' or 'ndvi'.
  • USE_P_SLOPE: enable or disable the optional slope-based (P) factor.
  • SCALE: set the analysis/export scale.
  • EXPORT_CRS: choose an appropriate projected coordinate reference system for your study area.

docs.text: The supplied screenshot is included in the site at docs/assets/images/rusle-erosion-map.png. It illustrates the map interface and erosion-class legend; it should be presented as an example output, not as independent validation of the model.

docs.title: Important limitations and validation
docs.text:
RUSLE estimates sheet and rill erosion under the assumptions encoded in its factors. It does not directly model gully erosion, sediment routing, or sediment delivery to streams. The factors and their parameter values should be checked against local literature and field observations.

Before interpreting results, pay particular attention to:

  • The rainfall-erosivity equation and its regional suitability.
  • Soil-property units and the assumptions used to derive (K).
  • The terrain data, flow accumulation interpretation, and LS-factor formulation.
  • The land-cover-to-(C) lookup values and the season represented by Sentinel-2 composites.
  • The (P)-factor values and whether they represent actual conservation practices.
  • The analysis scale and output projection.

Do not treat the map as field-validated soil loss. Validate the parameterization and results for the intended location before using them for planning or policy.

docs.title: JavaScript source
docs.text:
The complete script is available as a separate file and is shown below. Use the copy button on the code block to copy it into the Google Earth Engine Code Editor.

/*******************************************************************************
 * RUSLE SOIL LOSS MODEL - GOOGLE EARTH ENGINE (Code Editor, JavaScript)
 *
 *   A = R * K * LS * C * P      (t ha-1 yr-1)
 *
 *   R  Rainfall erosivity   CHIRPS daily rainfall -> Modified Fournier Index
 *                           R = 0.0739 * MFI^1.847  (Renard & Freimund, 1994)
 *   K  Soil erodibility     OpenLandMap sand/clay/organic carbon
 *                           EPIC equation (Williams, 1995), converted to SI
 *   LS Slope length-steepness  MERIT Hydro (elevation + upstream area)
 *                           Moore & Burch (1986) unit-stream-power formulation
 *   C  Cover management     Option 1: ESA WorldCover lookup table
 *                           Option 2: Sentinel-2 NDVI (van der Knijff et al.)
 *   P  Support practice     1 (none) or slope-based values for cropland
 *
 * REVISION NOTES (v2)
 *   - fCsand coefficient corrected (-0.0256, not -0.256)
 *   - R now averaged per year (Jensen's inequality bias removed)
 *   - A pinned to an explicit projected grid (was inheriting CHIRPS ~5.6 km)
 *   - Exports use an explicit EPSG code, not a server-side Projection object
 *   - K clamped to physical range; SCL mask tightened; slope smoothed
 *   - P table replaced with Wischmeier & Smith (1978) contour-farming values
 *
 * HOW TO USE: 1) Replace the AOI below. 2) Adjust the settings block.
 *             3) Click Run.
 ******************************************************************************/

// ============================ 1. SETTINGS ====================================

// AOI: example rectangle (replace with your own boundary).
// To use your own asset:  var aoi = ee.FeatureCollection('projects/ee-kwabenafosu/assets/Ghana').geometry();
var aoi = ee.Geometry.Rectangle([0.25, 6.35, 0.70, 6.85]);

var RAIN_START_YEAR = 2000;   // rainfall averaging period (>= 10-20 years recommended)
var RAIN_END_YEAR   = 2022;
var S2_YEAR         = 2023;   // year used for Sentinel-2 NDVI (C-factor option 2)

var C_METHOD    = 'landcover';  // 'landcover' or 'ndvi'
var USE_P_SLOPE = false;        // false: P = 1 everywhere; true: slope-based P on cropland
var LS_MAX      = 40;           // cap on LS to limit DEM/flow artefacts
var SCALE       = 90;           // analysis & export scale (m) - MERIT Hydro native ~90 m

// FIX: explicit export CRS. UTM 31N covers 0E-6E; change if you move the AOI.
var EXPORT_CRS  = 'EPSG:32631';

Map.centerObject(aoi, 10);

// ============================ 2. R FACTOR ====================================
// Modified Fournier Index per year: MFI = sum(monthly P^2) / annual P
//
// NOTE: the Renard & Freimund (1994) relation is a PER-YEAR relationship.
//       Because x^1.847 is convex, mean(MFI)^1.847 < mean(MFI^1.847), so we
//       compute R for each year and then average.
//
// PERF: this performs (years x 12) monthly reductions. For long periods it is
//       the slowest part of the script. Reduce RAIN_START_YEAR or coarsen the
//       AOI if the computation times out.

var chirps = ee.ImageCollection('UCSB-CHG/CHIRPS/DAILY').select('precipitation');
var years  = ee.List.sequence(RAIN_START_YEAR, RAIN_END_YEAR);
var months = ee.List.sequence(1, 12);

// Per-year R in MJ mm ha-1 h-1 yr-1
var rYearly = ee.ImageCollection.fromImages(
  years.map(function (y) {
    var monthly = ee.ImageCollection.fromImages(
      months.map(function (m) {
        var start = ee.Date.fromYMD(y, m, 1);
        return chirps.filterDate(start, start.advance(1, 'month'))
          .sum()
          .rename('P')
          .set('month', m);
      })
    );
    var sumSq = monthly.map(function (img) { return img.pow(2); }).sum();
    var total = monthly.sum();
    var mfi = sumSq.divide(total.max(1)).rename('MFI');
    return mfi.pow(1.847).multiply(0.0739).rename('R').set('year', y);
  })
);

var R = rYearly.mean().rename('R');   // mean annual R over the period

// Mean annual rainfall (mm) - reference only
var annualP = ee.ImageCollection.fromImages(
  years.map(function (y) {
    var start = ee.Date.fromYMD(y, 1, 1);
    return chirps.filterDate(start, start.advance(1, 'year')).sum()
      .rename('P').set('year', y);
  })
).mean();

// ============================ 3. K FACTOR ====================================
// FIX: Asset IDs corrected. The "-TOTAL-" variants do not exist in GEE.
//      The correct OpenLandMap assets use "-WFRACTION-".

// OpenLandMap topsoil (mean of 0 cm and 10 cm layers), 250 m
// Sand fraction [%w] - values are 1-100 (already in %)
var sand = ee.Image('OpenLandMap/SOL/SOL_SAND-WFRACTION_USDA-3A1A1A_M/v02')
  .select(['b0', 'b10']).reduce(ee.Reducer.mean()).rename('sand');   // %

// Clay fraction [%w] - values are 1-100 (already in %)
var clay = ee.Image('OpenLandMap/SOL/SOL_CLAY-WFRACTION_USDA-3A1A1A_M/v02')
  .select(['b0', 'b10']).reduce(ee.Reducer.mean()).rename('clay');   // %

var silt = ee.Image(100).subtract(sand).subtract(clay).max(0).rename('silt');

// Organic carbon: dataset is stored as "x 5 g/kg"  ->  % = value * 5 / 10
// This asset ID is correct; no change needed here.
var oc = ee.Image('OpenLandMap/SOL/SOL_ORGANIC-CARBON_USDA-6A1C_M/v02')
  .select(['b0', 'b10']).reduce(ee.Reducer.mean())
  .multiply(0.5).max(0.01).rename('oc');                              // % OC

// Williams (1995) EPIC equation
//   f_csand = 0.2 + 0.3 * exp(-0.0256 * Sa * (1 - Si/100))
var fCsand = ee.Image(0.2).add(
  sand.multiply(ee.Image(1).subtract(silt.divide(100)))
    .multiply(-0.0256).exp().multiply(0.3)
);

// f_clsi = (Si / (Cl + Si))^0.3
var fClSi = silt.divide(clay.add(silt).max(0.01)).pow(0.3);

// f_orgc = 1 - 0.25*OC / (OC + exp(3.72 - 2.95*OC))
var fOrgC = ee.Image(1).subtract(
  oc.multiply(0.25).divide(
    oc.add(oc.multiply(-2.95).add(3.72).exp())
  )
);

// f_hisand = 1 - 0.7*sn / (sn + exp(-5.51 + 22.9*sn)),  sn = 1 - Sa/100
var sn = ee.Image(1).subtract(sand.divide(100));
var fHiSand = ee.Image(1).subtract(
  sn.multiply(0.7).divide(
    sn.add(sn.multiply(22.9).add(-5.51).exp())
  )
);

// 0.1317 converts US units to SI: t ha h ha-1 MJ-1 mm-1
// Clamped to a physical range so EPIC outliers cannot propagate into A.
var K = fCsand.multiply(fClSi).multiply(fOrgC).multiply(fHiSand)
  .multiply(0.1317).max(0).min(0.7).rename('K');

// ============================ 4. LS FACTOR ===================================
var merit = ee.Image('MERIT/Hydro/v1_0_1');
var elv   = merit.select('elv');
var proj  = elv.projection();

// FIX: smooth the DEM before computing slope. Raw 90 m MERIT slope is noisy
// and biases LS upward. Radius 1 pixel is a light 3x3 mean.
var elvSmooth = elv.focal_mean({radius: 1, units: 'pixels', iterations: 1});

// Fixed projection so slope does not change with map zoom level.
// FIX: pass the scale explicitly (was reproject(proj) with no scale).
var slopeDeg = ee.Terrain.slope(elvSmooth)
  .reproject({crs: proj, scale: SCALE})
  .rename('slope');
var slopeRad = slopeDeg.multiply(Math.PI / 180);
var sinSlope = slopeRad.sin().max(0.001);

// Specific catchment area (m2 per m of contour width); upa is in km2
var As = merit.select('upa').multiply(1e6).divide(SCALE).max(SCALE);

// Moore & Burch (1986): LS = (As/22.13)^0.4 * (sin(slope)/0.0896)^1.3
var LS = As.divide(22.13).pow(0.4)
  .multiply(sinSlope.divide(0.0896).pow(1.3))
  .min(LS_MAX).max(0).rename('LS');

// ============================ 5. C FACTOR ====================================
// NOTE: ESA WorldCover v200 is a 2021 static product.
var lc = ee.ImageCollection('ESA/WorldCover/v200').first().select('Map');

var C;
if (C_METHOD === 'landcover') {
  // WorldCover classes: 10 tree, 20 shrub, 30 grass, 40 crop, 50 built, 60 bare,
  // 70 snow/ice, 80 water, 90 wetland, 95 mangrove, 100 moss/lichen
  // Literature-based values - adjust for your study area.
  var lcClasses = [10,   20,   30,   40,   50,   60,   70,  80,  90,   95,    100];
  var cValues   = [0.01, 0.03, 0.05, 0.30, 0.00, 0.50, 0.0, 0.0, 0.01, 0.001, 0.05];
  C = lc.remap(lcClasses, cValues, 0.1).rename('C');
} else {
  var s2 = ee.ImageCollection('COPERNICUS/S2_SR_HARMONIZED')
    .filterBounds(aoi)
    .filterDate(S2_YEAR + '-01-01', S2_YEAR + '-12-31')
    .filter(ee.Filter.lt('CLOUDY_PIXEL_PERCENTAGE', 40))
    .map(function (img) {
      // FIX: also mask nodata (0), saturated (1) and snow/ice (11),
      //      which the original mask left in.
      var scl = img.select('SCL');
      var good = scl.neq(0).and(scl.neq(1)).and(scl.neq(3))
        .and(scl.neq(8)).and(scl.neq(9)).and(scl.neq(10)).and(scl.neq(11));
      return img.normalizedDifference(['B8', 'B4'])
        .rename('NDVI').updateMask(good);
    });

  // NOTE: a full-year median blends dry- and rainy-season cover. In West
  //       Africa the erosive season is the rainy season, so consider a
  //       rainy-season composite here if your study area has a strong
  //       monsoonal cycle.
  var ndvi = s2.median().clamp(0, 0.99);
  // van der Knijff et al. (2000), alpha = 2, beta = 1
  C = ndvi.multiply(-2).divide(ee.Image(1).subtract(ndvi)).exp().rename('C');
}

// ============================ 6. P FACTOR ====================================
var P;
if (USE_P_SLOPE) {
  var slopePct = slopeRad.tan().multiply(100);

  // FIX: replaced with the actual Wischmeier & Smith (1978) Table 13
  //      contour-farming values. The originals (0.11, 0.12, 0.14, ...)
  //      are not from W&S and are ~3x too aggressive.
  //      (For contour strip-cropping use 0.30/0.25/0.25/0.30/0.35/0.40/0.45/0.55.)
  var pCrop = ee.Image(1.00)          // > 25%
    .where(slopePct.lte(25), 0.90)    // 21-25%
    .where(slopePct.lte(20), 0.80)    // 17-20%
    .where(slopePct.lte(16), 0.70)    // 13-16%
    .where(slopePct.lte(12), 0.60)    // 9-12%
    .where(slopePct.lte(8),  0.50)    // 6-8%
    .where(slopePct.lte(5),  0.50)    // 3-5%
    .where(slopePct.lte(2),  0.60);   // 1-2%

  P = ee.Image(1).where(lc.eq(40), pCrop).rename('P');
} else {
  P = ee.Image(1).rename('P');
}

// ============================ 7. SOIL LOSS ===================================
var notWater = lc.neq(80);

// FIX: pin the output grid explicitly. Without this, GEE takes the projection
// of the FIRST image in the expression (R, i.e. CHIRPS ~5.6 km) and silently
// evaluates everything on that grid.
var A = R.multiply(K).multiply(LS).multiply(C).multiply(P)
  .updateMask(notWater)
  .rename('A')
  .setDefaultProjection(proj, null, SCALE)
  .clip(aoi);

// Erosion severity classes (t ha-1 yr-1)
// 1 Very low <5 | 2 Low 5-15 | 3 Moderate 15-30 | 4 High 30-50
// 5 Very high 50-100 | 6 Severe >100
var classes = ee.Image(1)
  .where(A.gte(5),   2)
  .where(A.gte(15),  3)
  .where(A.gte(30),  4)
  .where(A.gte(50),  5)
  .where(A.gte(100), 6)
  .updateMask(A.mask())
  .rename('class')
  .setDefaultProjection(proj, null, SCALE)
  .clip(aoi);

// ============================ 8. MAP LAYERS ==================================
Map.addLayer(R.clip(aoi),  {min: 300, max: 1500, palette: ['#ffffcc', '#41b6c4', '#0c2c84']}, 'R factor', false);
Map.addLayer(K.clip(aoi),  {min: 0.01, max: 0.06, palette: ['#ffffe5', '#fe9929', '#662506']}, 'K factor', false);
Map.addLayer(LS.clip(aoi), {min: 0, max: 10, palette: ['#f7fcf5', '#74c476', '#00441b']}, 'LS factor', false);
Map.addLayer(C.clip(aoi),  {min: 0, max: 0.5, palette: ['#006400', '#ffff00', '#a52a2a']}, 'C factor', false);
Map.addLayer(P.clip(aoi),  {min: 0, max: 1, palette: ['#ffffff', '#555555']}, 'P factor', false);

Map.addLayer(A, {min: 0, max: 50,
  palette: ['#1a9850', '#91cf60', '#d9ef8b', '#fee08b', '#fc8d59', '#d73027', '#7f0000']},
  'Soil loss A (t/ha/yr)');
Map.addLayer(classes, {min: 1, max: 6,
  palette: ['#1a9850', '#a6d96a', '#ffffbf', '#fdae61', '#f46d43', '#a50026']},
  'Erosion classes', false);

// Legend
var legend = ui.Panel({style: {position: 'bottom-left', padding: '8px 12px'}});
legend.add(ui.Label('Erosion class (t/ha/yr)', {fontWeight: 'bold'}));
var legendItems = [
  ['#1a9850', 'Very low (<5)'], ['#a6d96a', 'Low (5-15)'], ['#ffffbf', 'Moderate (15-30)'],
  ['#fdae61', 'High (30-50)'], ['#f46d43', 'Very high (50-100)'], ['#a50026', 'Severe (>100)']
];
legendItems.forEach(function (it) {
  legend.add(ui.Panel([
    ui.Label('', {backgroundColor: it[0], padding: '8px', margin: '0 6px 4px 0'}),
    ui.Label(it[1], {margin: '0 0 4px 0'})
  ], ui.Panel.Layout.Flow('horizontal')));
});
Map.add(legend);

// ============================ 9. STATISTICS ==================================
// FIX: dropped bestEffort:true (it silently coarsens the requested scale).
var stats = A.reduceRegion({
  reducer: ee.Reducer.mean()
    .combine(ee.Reducer.median(), '', true)
    .combine(ee.Reducer.max(), '', true),
  geometry: aoi, scale: SCALE, maxPixels: 1e13
});
print('Soil loss A (t/ha/yr): mean / median / max', stats);

// Total soil loss (tonnes per year) = sum(A * pixel area in ha)
var totalLoss = A.multiply(ee.Image.pixelArea().divide(1e4)).reduceRegion({
  reducer: ee.Reducer.sum(), geometry: aoi, scale: SCALE, maxPixels: 1e13
});
print('Total soil loss (t/yr)', totalLoss);

// Area (ha) per erosion class
var areaByClass = ee.Image.pixelArea().divide(1e4).addBands(classes).reduceRegion({
  reducer: ee.Reducer.sum().group({groupField: 1, groupName: 'class'}),
  geometry: aoi, scale: SCALE, maxPixels: 1e13
});
print('Area (ha) by erosion class (1=very low ... 6=severe)', areaByClass);

// Mean annual rainfall for reference
// NOTE: 5566 m is the CHIRPS native resolution - keep it here on purpose.
print('Mean annual rainfall (mm)', annualP.reduceRegion({
  reducer: ee.Reducer.mean(), geometry: aoi, scale: 5566, maxPixels: 1e13
}));

// Sanity check on the K factor (should be ~0.005-0.07 for most soils)
print('K factor stats', K.reduceRegion({
  reducer: ee.Reducer.minMax().combine(ee.Reducer.mean(), '', true),
  geometry: aoi, scale: SCALE, maxPixels: 1e13
}));

// Per-year R, for a quick sanity check against your rainfall regime
print('Per-year R (MJ mm ha-1 h-1 yr-1)', rYearly.aggregate_array('R'));

// ============================ 10. EXPORTS ====================================
// FIX: crs is now an explicit EPSG string, not a server-side Projection object.
Export.image.toDrive({
  image: A.toFloat(), description: 'RUSLE_soil_loss_t_ha_yr', folder: 'GEE_RUSLE',
  region: aoi, scale: SCALE, crs: EXPORT_CRS, maxPixels: 1e13
});
Export.image.toDrive({
  image: classes.toByte(), description: 'RUSLE_erosion_classes', folder: 'GEE_RUSLE',
  region: aoi, scale: SCALE, crs: EXPORT_CRS, maxPixels: 1e13
});
Export.image.toDrive({
  image: ee.Image.cat([R, K, LS, C, P]).clip(aoi).toFloat(),
  description: 'RUSLE_factors_R_K_LS_C_P', folder: 'GEE_RUSLE',
  region: aoi, scale: SCALE, crs: EXPORT_CRS, maxPixels: 1e13
});

docs.title: Water Budget and Storage-Change Analysis

Google Earth Engine · JavaScript · Hydrology · Remote Sensing

A basin-scale workflow for estimating the water budget and comparing budget-derived storage change with storage change estimated from GLDAS.

View JavaScript source Explore the workflow

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
The water budget describes how precipitation, evapotranspiration, runoff, and changes in water storage relate over a defined area and time interval.

The workflow calculates:

[ \Delta S_{\text{budget}} = P - ET - Q ]

It then compares the budget-derived storage change with an independent estimate based on changes in GLDAS storage variables:

[ \text{Closure error} = \Delta S_{\text{budget}} - \Delta S_{\text{GLDAS}} ]

A nonzero closure error indicates disagreement between the two estimates. It can reflect measurement uncertainty, model limitations, spatial or temporal mismatches, missing data, and omitted processes.

docs.title: 3. Workflow
docs.text:
1. Define the area of interest and analysis period.
  2. Load and preprocess the precipitation, ET, and GLDAS datasets.
  3. Aggregate the selected components to monthly intervals.
  4. Estimate storage change from the water-budget equation.
  5. Calculate GLDAS-based storage change and closure error.
  6. Generate basin-average monthly, annual, and climatological summaries.
  7. Visualize mean annual water-budget components.
  8. Export summary tables and raster outputs to Google Drive.

docs.text:

  • Annual water-budget summary.
  • Monthly climatology.

  • CSV and GeoTIFF export tasks.

docs.title: 5. Configuration
docs.text:
The supplied script uses a rectangular example study area and the 2015–2020 analysis period. Replace the example geometry with your study basin before interpreting results.

The evapotranspiration source can be set to MODIS or TERRACLIMATE.

docs.title: 6. JavaScript source code
docs.text:
The complete JavaScript file is available as a separate file and is shown below. Use the copy button on the code block to copy it into the Google Earth Engine Code Editor.

/*******************************************************************************
 * PROJECT: WATER BUDGET AND STORAGE-CHANGE ANALYSIS
 * PLATFORM: Google Earth Engine Code Editor
 * LANGUAGE: JavaScript
 *
 * WATER-BUDGET EQUATION
 *   P = ET + Q + dS
 *   dS_budget = P - ET - Q
 *
 * VARIABLES
 *   P          Precipitation (mm)
 *   ET         Evapotranspiration (mm)
 *   Q          Surface + subsurface runoff (mm)
 *   dS_budget  Budget-derived storage change (mm)
 *   dS_gldas   GLDAS storage change (mm)
 *   closure    Difference between the two storage estimates (mm)
 *
 * DATASETS
 *   Precipitation: CHIRPS Daily
 *   ET: MODIS MOD16A2GF or TerraClimate AET
 *   Runoff/storage: GLDAS-2.1 NOAH
 *
 * OUTPUTS
 *   Monthly/annual/climatology tables, charts, mean-annual maps,
 *   CSV exports, and a GeoTIFF export.
 *
 * HOW TO USE
 *   1. Replace the example AOI with your basin.
 *   2. Set START_YEAR, END_YEAR, and ET_SOURCE.
 *   3. Run the script and start export tasks in the Tasks panel.
 *
 * IMPORTANT
 *   Verify dataset units, temporal aggregation, and boundary-date coverage
 *   before interpreting the results scientifically.
 *
 * Author: Godwin Ebo Fosu
 ******************************************************************************/

// ============================ 1. SETTINGS ====================================

// Example AOI. Replace with your basin, or use an Earth Engine asset:
// var aoi = ee.FeatureCollection('projects/your-project/assets/basin').geometry();
var aoi = ee.Geometry.Rectangle([0.25, 6.35, 0.70, 6.85]);

var START_YEAR = 2015;
var END_YEAR   = 2020;        // GLDAS needs data through the next year boundary
var ET_SOURCE  = 'MODIS';     // 'MODIS' or 'TERRACLIMATE'
var ANALYSIS_SCALE = 1000;    // metres for basin averaging

Map.centerObject(aoi, 9);

var nYears  = END_YEAR - START_YEAR + 1;
var nMonths = nYears * 12;
var startDate = ee.Date.fromYMD(START_YEAR, 1, 1);

// ============================ 2. DATASETS ====================================

var chirps = ee.ImageCollection('UCSB-CHG/CHIRPS/DAILY')
  .select('precipitation');

var gldas = ee.ImageCollection('NASA/GLDAS/V021/NOAH/G025/T3H')
  .filterDate(START_YEAR + '-01-01', (END_YEAR + 1) + '-01-02');

// MODIS ET: scale factor 0.1. This converts each 8-day composite total
// into an approximate daily rate; validate the final composite duration.
var modisDaily = ee.ImageCollection('MODIS/061/MOD16A2GF')
  .filterDate(START_YEAR + '-01-01', (END_YEAR + 1) + '-01-01')
  .select('ET')
  .map(function (img) {
    var t0 = ee.Date(img.get('system:time_start'));
    var nextYear = ee.Date.fromYMD(t0.get('year').add(1), 1, 1);
    var days = ee.Number(8).min(nextYear.difference(t0, 'day'));
    return img.multiply(0.1).divide(days)
      .rename('ET_day')
      .toFloat()
      .set('system:time_start', t0.millis());
  });

var terra = ee.ImageCollection('IDAHO_EPSCOR/TERRACLIMATE')
  .select('aet');

// ============================ 3. HELPERS =====================================

// Total selected GLDAS water storage components (mm = kg/m2)
function storage(img) {
  return img.select('SoilMoi0_10cm_inst')
    .add(img.select('SoilMoi10_40cm_inst'))
    .add(img.select('SoilMoi40_100cm_inst'))
    .add(img.select('SoilMoi100_200cm_inst'))
    .add(img.select('SWE_inst'))
    .add(img.select('CanopInt_inst'))
    .rename('S')
    .toFloat();
}

// First 3-hourly GLDAS image at/after a date (00:00 UTC).
// Confirm that an image exists at the requested boundary date.
function gldasAt(date) {
  return ee.Image(gldas.filterDate(date, date.advance(3, 'hour')).first());
}

// ============================ 4. MONTHLY WATER BUDGET ========================

function monthlyBudget(i) {
  i = ee.Number(i);
  var start = startDate.advance(i, 'month');
  var end   = start.advance(1, 'month');
  var daysInMonth = end.difference(start, 'day');

  // Precipitation (mm/month)
  var P = chirps.filterDate(start, end).sum().rename('P').toFloat();

  // ET (mm/month). Confirm source-specific scale factors and aggregation.
  var ET;
  if (ET_SOURCE === 'MODIS') {
    ET = modisDaily.filterDate(start, end).mean()
      .multiply(daysInMonth).rename('ET').toFloat();
  } else {
    // TerraClimate AET is typically scaled by 0.1; verify current catalog docs.
    ET = ee.Image(terra.filterDate(start, end).first())
      .multiply(0.1).rename('ET').toFloat();
  }

  // GLDAS runoff: inspect band units and temporal accumulation semantics.
  var qSum = gldas.filterDate(start, end)
    .select(['Qs_acc', 'Qsb_acc']).sum();
  var Q = qSum.select('Qs_acc').add(qSum.select('Qsb_acc'))
    .rename('Q').toFloat();

  // Storage change between interval boundaries.
  var dSgldas = storage(gldasAt(end)).subtract(storage(gldasAt(start)))
    .rename('dS_gldas').toFloat();

  // Use ET's valid pixels for all components.
  var valid = ET.mask();
  P = P.updateMask(valid);
  Q = Q.updateMask(valid);
  dSgldas = dSgldas.updateMask(valid);

  var dSbudget = P.subtract(ET).subtract(Q).rename('dS_budget').toFloat();
  var closure  = dSbudget.subtract(dSgldas).rename('closure').toFloat();

  return ee.Image.cat([P, ET, Q, dSbudget, dSgldas, closure])
    .set({
      'system:time_start': start.millis(),
      'year': start.get('year'),
      'month': start.get('month')
    });
}

var monthlyCol = ee.ImageCollection.fromImages(
  ee.List.sequence(0, nMonths - 1).map(monthlyBudget)
);

// ============================ 5. BASIN AVERAGES ==============================

function basinMean(img) {
  return img.reduceRegion({
    reducer: ee.Reducer.mean(),
    geometry: aoi,
    scale: ANALYSIS_SCALE,
    maxPixels: 1e13,
    bestEffort: true
  });
}

// Monthly table
var monthlyFC = monthlyCol.map(function (img) {
  return ee.Feature(null, basinMean(img)).set({
    'date': ee.Date(img.get('system:time_start')).format('YYYY-MM'),
    'system:time_start': img.get('system:time_start'),
    'year': img.get('year'),
    'month': img.get('month')
  });
});

// Annual table (sum of monthly image values)
var annualFC = ee.FeatureCollection(
  ee.List.sequence(START_YEAR, END_YEAR).map(function (y) {
    var img = monthlyCol.filter(ee.Filter.eq('year', y)).sum();
    return ee.Feature(null, basinMean(img))
      .set('year', ee.Number(y).format('%d'));
  })
);

// Monthly climatology (mean of each calendar month)
var climFC = ee.FeatureCollection(
  ee.List.sequence(1, 12).map(function (m) {
    var img = monthlyCol.filter(ee.Filter.eq('month', m)).mean();
    return ee.Feature(null, basinMean(img))
      .set('month', ee.Number(m).format('%02d'));
  })
);

// ============================ 6. CHARTS & PRINTS =============================

print('Basin area (km2)', aoi.area(1).divide(1e6));
print('Annual water budget (mm/yr)', annualFC);

print(ui.Chart.feature.byFeature(monthlyFC, 'date', ['P', 'ET', 'Q'])
  .setChartType('LineChart')
  .setOptions({
    title: 'Monthly P, ET and Q (basin mean)',
    vAxis: {title: 'mm / month'},
    hAxis: {title: 'Month', slantedText: true},
    lineWidth: 2,
    pointSize: 0
  }));

print(ui.Chart.feature.byFeature(annualFC, 'year', ['P', 'ET', 'Q', 'dS_budget'])
  .setChartType('ColumnChart')
  .setOptions({
    title: 'Annual water budget components',
    vAxis: {title: 'mm / year'},
    hAxis: {title: 'Year'}
  }));

print(ui.Chart.feature.byFeature(climFC, 'month', ['P', 'ET', 'Q'])
  .setChartType('ColumnChart')
  .setOptions({
    title: 'Mean monthly climatology',
    vAxis: {title: 'mm / month'},
    hAxis: {title: 'Month'}
  }));

print(ui.Chart.feature.byFeature(monthlyFC, 'date',
  ['dS_budget', 'dS_gldas', 'closure'])
  .setChartType('LineChart')
  .setOptions({
    title: 'Storage change: budget vs GLDAS and closure error',
    vAxis: {title: 'mm / month'},
    hAxis: {title: 'Month', slantedText: true},
    lineWidth: 2,
    pointSize: 0
  }));

// ============================ 7. MAPS ========================================

// Mean annual values over the analysis period (mm/year)
var meanAnnual = monthlyCol.select(['P', 'ET', 'Q', 'dS_budget'])
  .sum().divide(nYears).clip(aoi);

Map.addLayer(meanAnnual.select('P'),
  {min: 800, max: 1600,
   palette: ['#ffffd9', '#7fcdbb', '#1d91c0', '#081d58']},
  'Mean annual P (mm)');

Map.addLayer(meanAnnual.select('ET'),
  {min: 500, max: 1400,
   palette: ['#ffffe5', '#addd8e', '#31a354', '#004529']},
  'Mean annual ET (mm)', false);

Map.addLayer(meanAnnual.select('Q'),
  {min: 0, max: 400,
   palette: ['#f7fbff', '#6baed6', '#08306b']},
  'Mean annual Q (mm)', false);

Map.addLayer(meanAnnual.select('dS_budget'),
  {min: -100, max: 600,
   palette: ['#d73027', '#ffffbf', '#1a9850']},
  'Mean annual P-ET-Q (mm)', false);

Map.addLayer(ee.Image().byte().paint(aoi, 0, 2),
  {palette: 'black'}, 'AOI');

// ============================ 8. EXPORTS =====================================

Export.table.toDrive({
  collection: monthlyFC,
  description: 'WaterBudget_monthly',
  folder: 'GEE_WaterBudget',
  fileFormat: 'CSV',
  selectors: [
    'date', 'year', 'month', 'P', 'ET', 'Q',
    'dS_budget', 'dS_gldas', 'closure'
  ]
});

Export.table.toDrive({
  collection: annualFC,
  description: 'WaterBudget_annual',
  folder: 'GEE_WaterBudget',
  fileFormat: 'CSV',
  selectors: ['year', 'P', 'ET', 'Q', 'dS_budget', 'dS_gldas', 'closure']
});

Export.image.toDrive({
  image: meanAnnual.toFloat(),
  description: 'WaterBudget_mean_annual_maps',
  folder: 'GEE_WaterBudget',
  region: aoi,
  scale: 1000,
  maxPixels: 1e13
});

docs.title: 7. Important limitations
docs.text:
• Spatial resolution: CHIRPS, MODIS, TerraClimate, and GLDAS have different spatial resolutions. A common analysis scale does not make their native resolutions equivalent.
  • Temporal aggregation: The MODIS ET conversion and monthly aggregation should be validated against the composite timing and scale factors.
  • Runoff units: Verify the GLDAS runoff-band units and temporal accumulation semantics before interpreting monthly sums as millimetres.
  • Storage change: Storage differences require valid observations at the intended interval boundaries. Missing or masked observations can affect the result.
  • Water-budget assumptions: The simplified equation does not explicitly represent every possible inflow, outflow, or storage process.

Treat the outputs as model-based estimates and assess their uncertainty before using them for operational water-resource decisions.
